name: Count & Replenish — Store Inventory Frontline
archetype: Store-based roles whose daily rhythm shifts from manual reorder math and printed count sheets to managing system-generated replenishment exceptions on a tablet. The highest-volume, highest-churn audience in the program.
top_impacts: Automated replenishment replacing manual reorder spreadsheets
goals: Keep shelves stocked without lost sales from stockouts
Spend less of the morning on spreadsheet math and more on the floor
Trust that the numbers in the system match what is physically in the back room
pain_points: Manual weekly reorder-point calculations in spreadsheets, emailed as POs
No confidence the system accounts for local events (weather, promotions, school schedules)
Limited desk time — anything that requires sitting at a PC gets deferred
quote: The spreadsheet is mine — I know it's right because I built it. (Store lead, Retail Ops workshop)

journey.current: Walks the floor with a printed count sheet, keys quantities into a spreadsheet at the back-office PC.
journey.future: Scans shelf gaps on a tablet in-aisle; counts flow straight into the ERP.
journey.support: In-app guidance on the tablet count flow; laminated job aid at the receiving desk

journey.current: Calculates reorder points manually in the spreadsheet and emails POs weekly.
journey.future: Reviews system-generated replenishment suggestions and works only the exception queue.
journey.support: Coaching through the first two replenishment cycles; benefit narrative comms on why the suggestions can be trusted

journey.current: Adjusts orders by instinct for local events; the knowledge lives in the lead's head.
journey.future: Enters event overrides in the ERP so the demand signal learns; override history is visible to the team.
journey.support: VILT module on the override workflow; manager talking points acknowledging the expertise being encoded

journey.current: Chases mismatches between the emailed PO, the delivery, and the spreadsheet.
journey.future: System-matched receipts; exceptions surface automatically with a reason code.
journey.support: Job aid on exception reason codes; floor-walk support from champions in week 1

before.activity: Walks the floor with the printed count sheet, marking gaps by hand
Keys counts into the reorder spreadsheet at the back-office PC
Calculates reorder points, adjusts for the weekend promotion by instinct
Emails the weekly PO batch to suppliers; prints copies for the binder
Receives a delivery; chases a mismatch against last week's emailed PO
Back on the floor coaching associates; spreadsheet questions wait until tomorrow

after.activity: Walks the floor with the tablet; scans shelf gaps in-aisle
Reviews the overnight replenishment suggestions in the exception queue
Enters a weekend-promotion override so the demand signal accounts for it
Approves the suggestion batch; no PO emails, no binder
Receives a delivery; the one exception surfaces with a reason code
Extra floor time reclaimed — coaching associates on the new count flow

name: Plan & Buy — Buyers & Planners
archetype: Merchandising roles moving from instinct-driven Excel buying to a formal open-to-buy planning discipline in the ERP — a net-new capability, not a tool swap.
top_impacts: Open-to-buy financial planning introduced as net-new capability
goals: Buy the right assortment without ending the season in forced markdowns
Defend buying decisions with numbers, not just track record
Get through the first OTB cycle without missing a buying window
pain_points: No enterprise open-to-buy process today; plans live in personal Excel files
No shared view of committed vs. available budget across the buying team
Classroom training is hard to schedule during buying season

journey.current: Each buyer plans the season in a personal Excel file; totals reconcile only at review time.
journey.future: Season plan is built in the ERP planning module against a shared open-to-buy budget.
journey.support: ILT on OTB fundamentals before the tool; role-definition session on who owns which plan level

journey.current: Buys by instinct within a loose budget; over-commitment surfaces months later.
journey.future: Every buy checks against remaining open-to-buy in real time; over-commitment is blocked, not discovered.
journey.support: Coaching through the first OTB cycle; escalation path for legitimate budget exceptions

journey.current: Manual roll-up of Excel files for the review meeting; numbers are stale on arrival.
journey.future: Live OTB position drives the review; conversation shifts from reconciling to deciding.
journey.support: Job aid on the OTB review dashboard; leader talking points for the first live review

journey.current: Markdown decisions come late because over-buys are only visible at season end.
journey.future: Early markdown signals from the plan-vs-actual gap; markdowns are planned, not forced.
journey.support: Reinforcement comms tying OTB discipline to the markdown-avoidance benefit

before.activity: Opens the personal season plan in Excel; updates last week's sales manually
Supplier call — commits to a buy based on instinct and the relationship
Emails the commitment to the assistant to log; the plan file is now out of date
Builds a roll-up for the review meeting from three versions of the file
Review meeting spent reconciling whose numbers are right

after.activity: Opens the ERP planning workspace; sales actuals are already in
Supplier call — checks remaining open-to-buy live before committing
Logs the buy in the ERP; the shared OTB position updates for the whole team
Reviews the plan-vs-actual gap the system flagged for two categories
Review meeting spent deciding markdowns early, not reconciling spreadsheets

name: Account & Control — Finance Operations
archetype: Finance roles absorbing the downstream effects of automated replenishment and OTB discipline — cleaner POs and receipts, a shared budget position, and new month-end reconciliation inputs. Material change, but simpler journey than the frontline.
top_impacts: Automated replenishment replacing manual reorder spreadsheets
goals: Close the month without chasing store spreadsheets for PO backup
One version of the committed-spend number
pain_points: PO backup arrives as emailed spreadsheets in inconsistent formats
Committed spend is invisible until invoices land

name: Steer & Enable — Managers & Sponsors
archetype: Store and merchandising managers who must sponsor the change locally: run the new exception-review cadence, deliver talking points, and coach teams through the trust dip on system suggestions.
top_impacts: Automated replenishment replacing manual reorder spreadsheets
Open-to-buy financial planning introduced as net-new capability
goals: Keep team performance steady through cutover
Be credible answering 'why should I trust the system?'
pain_points: No shared view of team workload during the transition
Expected to sponsor a change they have not been trained on first

name: IT Support
archetype: Service-desk and device-support roles fielding tablet and login issues at go-live; covered by standard hypercare onboarding.

name: Warehouse Dispatch
archetype: Receives system-generated POs instead of emailed ones; process otherwise unchanged.

name: Internal Audit
archetype: New audit trail on overrides and OTB exceptions; informational briefing only.
